mappings.note: Affirms 'service sector' as the other name for tertiary; sector vocabulary, so LO-322.
Rejects the claim that AMUL was set up to enrich middlemen - a point about why the cooperative existed, so CG-SST4.
Milking as primary and butter-making as secondary; sector placement of two stages of the dairy chain, so LO-322.
Kautilya's line that economic activity is the root of prosperity and its absence brings distress: an ancient text (LO-311) on the economy (CG-SST4).
Asks why classification into sectors helps. The supplied answer has been overrun by a banking-is-tertiary key, but either reading is a sector item, so LO-322.
Rules out furniture-making from the primary list, keeping greenhouse farming, fishery and forestry - a sector-placement check, so LO-322.
Agriculture feeding food processing which relies on transport: interdependence across all three sectors, hence LO-322.
Finds 'mining - electricity production' false among farming, forestry and fishing outputs; the item turns on what each primary activity actually yields, so LO-322.
Sorts milking, cheese-making and supermarket selling into the three sectors and keeps only the second as secondary - sector placement, so LO-322.
Names the tertiary sector as the one complementing the other two; sector vocabulary and interdependence, so LO-322.
Sardar Patel's reason for advising a cooperative - to free farmers from middlemen: the purpose of an economic institution, so CG-SST4.
The socio-economic effect of AMUL on its members - higher income, shared ownership, democratic participation: the cooperative as an institution, hence CG-SST4.
How a failure of tree supply would ripple through papermaking, printing, transport and retail: interdependence across the sectors, so LO-322.
Recycling's saving of trees, energy and water argued for responsible consumption: conservation of natural resources (CG-SST1) achieved inside a secondary-sector activity (LO-322).
A collapse in tourism dragging down local farming and craft production - interdependence running from the tertiary sector back down, so LO-322.
Compares the nature of work and dependence on nature in primary against secondary work; the defining contrast between the sectors, so LO-322.
A farming app built by a software firm, and what happens when rural connectivity is weak: tertiary services supporting primary work, so LO-322.
Rajesh's expanding workshop traced through wood, tools and a delivery service: one business touching all three sectors, hence LO-322.
What secondary and tertiary activities could grow around a fishing village - processing, boat repair, ice, cold storage, tourism: sector development around a primary occupation, so LO-322.
Kautilya's warning explained through the chain linking the three sectors: the ancient text (LO-311) applied to sector interdependence (LO-322).

Why developing countries seek stronger secondary and tertiary sectors - higher value addition, more skilled work, greater stability: the mix of available occupations (LO-322) and the economy's structure (CG-SST4).
A drought hitting wheat farming and then flour mills, bakeries and hauliers in turn; the clearest interdependence case in the chapter, so LO-322.
A fish canning and export unit adding value to a fishing community, with cold storage and shipping behind it: the sector chain (LO-322) and the new enterprise's effect on the local economy (CG-SST4).
